## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Retain every original vertex, including isolated vertices. Enumerate the forbidden-copy vertex sets in n^{O_H(1)} time. An empty graph has exactly one deletion set, the empty set. A requested size outside [0,n] has count zero.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n)$ |
| Clauses | $O_{\mathcal H}(n^h+n)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{h,3\}$ |

## Derivation

1. Use one deletion bit x_v for each original vertex. For every vertex set S supporting a forbidden copy, add $\bigvee_{v\in S}x_v$. Duplicate copies on the same S may share one clause. No gate or auxiliary variable is introduced for a forbidden copy.

2. Vertex deletion keeps the adjacency relation among surviving vertices unchanged. Hence G−D is free of the specified induced or ordinary copies exactly when D meets every forbidden copy in the original graph. This establishes a bijection between deletion sets and satisfying assignments of the selection bits.

3. There are O_H(n^h) copy clauses, each of width at most h. For size t add $\sum_v x_v=t$ using the linear-size adder of METHODS.md Section 2, with full gate equivalences. It adds O(n) variables and clauses, and every eligible deletion set has exactly one extension.

4. Thus N=O(n), M=O_H(n^h+n), and w≤max(h,3). The encoded bit length is O_H((n^h+n) log(n+2)); construction is polynomial for the fixed family. Apply the general-density exact-counting assumption to obtain A(n)L^{O(1)}, with polynomial space. The separately reported formalization profile gives its own displayed weaker alternative.

5. All sizes can be counted with n+1 queries. The smallest size with nonzero count is the optimum deletion size; its count is the number of optimum deletion sets, and comparing it with one decides optimum uniqueness. These polynomially many calls do not change the exponential factor. See the separate optimization entry for witness reconstruction.

6. For induced copies, H={P3} gives Cluster Vertex Deletion; for ordinary copies, H={K2} gives Vertex Cover. These are examples of the direct counting construction, without a decision kernel. METHODS.md Section 3 explains the distinction from solution-budget FPT transfers.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The finite family, its largest order h, and the induced/noninduced convention are fixed independently of the input. Enumerating arbitrary input patterns is outside this entry.
- The scale is the original vertex count n, not the deletion budget. A linear vertex kernel is unnecessary here, and an ordinary decision kernel cannot be inserted into this counting argument without a separate count-preservation proof.
- Fixed forbidden minors are not covered by the copy-enumeration argument: a minor model can use unboundedly many vertices. Edge additions, deletions, or editing can create forbidden copies and require a separate analysis.
- No binary-weight or inclusion-minimal-deletion counting claim is made by this entry. The clauses remain at their fixed width; splitting every constant-width clause into 3-clauses can unnecessarily increase the variable count.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
